reason: The draft answers Marisol's question directly and honestly: skip the 16-miler, because a long run this close to the race adds no fitness and risks flat legs, a calf strain and lost glycogen. That is the safe and correct call. The plan follows her schedule: Monday and Friday off, the session on Wednesday and five run days, with Sunday as the race. Running before the race comes to about 15 mi after a 34 mi week, so it's a sensible taper with no jumps. A short dose of marathon-pace work on Wednesday, plus strides, keeps her legs sharp without tiring them. The 8:35/mi pace matches a sub-3:45 finish, and opening the first 10 miles at 8:40 is sound pacing advice. Every day can be run as written. No must-never check is triggered. Nothing hurts, and her heavy legs read as normal taper staleness, not exhaustion. Docked one point because the visible text barely speaks to her nerves and her fear of losing fitness. It also never tells her that heavy, flat legs are normal in a taper, which is the reassurance she most needs. The draft also assumes race day is Sunday, which the card implies but never states.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 53, 40, 42, 46 mi
This week: 34 mi over 5 runs.
Body: "Legs heavy and flat. Nothing hurts, they just feel dead."
Feeling: "Nervous. I feel like I'm losing fitness."
Asks: "Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: This is race week, so the plan is short, sharp, and built to put you on the start line fresh. …
Answers: No, please skip the 16-miler. A long run this close to race day cannot add fitness, but it can leave your legs flat on Sunday, nick a calf, or chew into the glycogen you want to start the race with.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off to kick the taper week into gear.
Tue: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145, then 4 x 20-second strides. Keeps the legs…
Wed: easy, 5 mi, with 3 x 1 mi at marathon pace (8:35/mi), full easy jog between. A…
Thu: easy, 3 mi, very relaxed, heart rate under 140. Short shakeout, nothing more.
Fri: rest. Stay off your feet where you can and start loading carbs and fluids.
Sat: easy, 2 mi, with 4 x 20-second strides at the end. Opens the legs the day before…
Sun: race, 26.2 mi, target under 3:45 (8:35/mi), ease into the first 10 at 8:40…
